- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from bullish to bearish, delay forecast drop by 1–3 days and reduce slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply mean reversion bias: if 10-day moving avg is > forecast, reduce forecast by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows volatility, model overpredicts volatility; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% for next 7 days.
